system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)

- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

Prepared for the Wattlebridge Holdings deal team. All Seller material treated as the counterparty's draft; assessed against the Buyer Playbook only. Note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter (paras 2–10) repeatedly undercuts the Seller Update's assertions – those admissions should be used.

| Ref | Issue | Seller position | Buyer wants | Recommendation | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1) | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 | **REJECT – hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m** | 20% is our fallback only; no Amelia Frost written authority has been given for this draft. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2) | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded | **REJECT – counter at playbook figures, tipping basket** | Seller's thresholds are 5x ours on both limbs and switch to deductible recovery, which materially dilutes the warranty package. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months post-Completion; limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated" (cl 12.3/13) | 24 months; limitation applies only to general Warranty Claims | **REJECT – hold 24 months; delete the "all Claims" default** | 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the "all Claims" language is a backdoor override of the separate regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% of price cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **REJECT outright** | Collapsing title into a 20%/18-month regime would leave 80% of the price unrecoverable on a defective-title claim; "simplicity" is not a reason. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | **REJECT – insert express carve-out; non-negotiable** | No cap on fraud is a market and legal baseline (NSW law) and the playbook prohibits anyone waiving it. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012), accounts, registers and public records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure | **REJECT – require fair, specific disclosure with sufficient detail to identify nature and scope** | Whole-data-room disclosure would gut the warranties, especially given DL 1.4 disclaims any admission on every matter. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | No claim for any matter the Buyer or advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records (cl 8.3) | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | **REJECT – delete cl 8.3** | "Discoverable" constructive knowledge plus adviser imputation shifts DD risk entirely to Buyer and overlaps with the deemed-disclosure attack in SPA-N-006. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of written consent (cl 3/6.3) | Condition precedent: effective consent AND evidence cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, before Completion | **REJECT – redraft as CP requiring effective, unconditional (or conditions-evidenced) consent** | DL para 2 admits no final consent and no evidence of conditions; reasonable endeavours and consent-on-delivery are insufficient for a AUD 3.6m customer. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) | Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7) | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion | **REJECT – require payout letter, funds-flow repayment and executed releases as Completion deliverables** | DL para 3 confirms not repaid and no discharge; a post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000) | "A matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow | Specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded, including payroll tax, super and on-costs triggered | **REJECT – add line item (AUD 420,000 + on-costs) as Seller cost / Debt-like item** | DL para 5 confirms the bonuses are Completion-triggered and absent from the funds flow; silence means the Buyer pays them post-Completion under a debt-free/cash-free price. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Limited to SOW3 payment only; "adequate" (cl 11.1) | Broader indemnity covering title to/transfer of SOW3 Project Materials, claims and remediation costs, while preserving the cure (cleared payment under cl 7.3) | **COUNTER – broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure mechanism** | DL para 4 admits no receipt or confirmatory assignment exists, so IP ownership is contingent; the AUD 180,000 figure is unverified either way, so do not price it as settled. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident (DD-006) | "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6) | Log preservation, proper investigation, update obligations and a specific indemnity/warranty on the outcome; no assumption of breach or non-breach | **COUNTER – covenants to preserve, investigate and update to Completion; specific indemnity; no numeric adjustment yet** | DL para 6 confirms ~1,240 records and an unresolved investigation; neither side can yet establish access, scope or notification duty, so the Seller's "not material" label is premature. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | Ordinary-course operating costs | Assessment of whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course before classification | **ASSESS – no automatic Debt classification or price deduction; request DD-008/DD-011 analysis and termination rights** | DL para 8 admits the Seller does not know the status of each renewal; the three related contracts should be read together before any accept/reject. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"; "all Claims" default in cl 12.3/13 and 9.3/12.8/20.5 | Title / Tax / IP / payment / covenant / specific-indemnity categories kept separate with their own limits; no hidden general-regime override | **REJECT – add express hierarchy clause: general limits apply only to general Warranty Claims** | Three separate drafting devices in the Seller Update attempt to fold every category into the 20%/18-month regime. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012 | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority (ASIC searches, PPSR, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, officer/solicitor certificates) | **REJECT as sufficient – obtain independent verification before Completion** | DL para 10 concedes DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal source and that no Buyer verification has occurred; a share register is not independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax / IP open terms | "Settled under the general regime" | Terms remain OPEN; separate Tax and IP regimes to be negotiated (caps, periods, specific indemnities), no unlimited liability assumed | **REJECT the "settled" characterisation – mark as OPEN** | Nothing has been agreed; the Seller is attempting to close these by assertion within the diluted general regime. |

## Overall assessment

The Seller Update is not a "fair and balanced package". It combines a sub-playbook cap (20%), 5x thresholds with deductible recovery, an 18-month period, and three separate override mechanisms (cl 12.3/13, cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, and the Tax/IP "settled" assertion) that would push title, tax, IP and even fraud under the general regime. The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Update and should be quoted back: it admits no Bluefen consent, no Riverlark discharge, no Ironquay assignment, unfunded bonuses, an unresolved privacy incident and non-independent title evidence.

**Priority items for the mark-up (in order):** SPA-N-005 (fraud), SPA-N-004/014 (regime separation), SPA-N-008 (Bluefen CP), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark at Completion), SPA-N-010 (bonus funding), then the economic terms at SPA-N-001–003.

**Approvals position:** No Amelia Frost written authority exists for either the 20% cap or the 18-month period. Both must be held at playbook positions in this round. No one on the deal team can agree the fraud carve-out away.
=== END ADVICE ===
